transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (QuantumCore Partnerships), Lina Zhao (QuantumCore Head of Solutions), Dr. Eva Müller (QuantumCore Solutions Architect)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Quick partner intro; Redwood gives overview of inference product and dedicated/private options; QuantumCore explains they are a GPU/cloud provider interested in go-to-market and technical integration; action items to share docs and schedule deep-dive and benchmarks.

00:00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, really excited to get to know the QuantumCore team — I think this is, yeah, a great place to start. I'm Alex, I'm on the partnerships/AE side at Redwood.
00:00:12 Marco Ruiz: Hi Alex, Marco here; thanks for setting this up. We're exploring partnerships with a couple of inference platforms and Redwood came highly recommended.
00:00:20 Priya Patel: hey everyone, Priya here, I'm the SE, I'll focus on the technical integration stuff and run the benchmarks with your team.
00:00:28 Lina Zhao: Lina from QuantumCore, hi - we'll be looking at potential channel and joint go-to-market, also how the integration looks from an ops perspective.
00:00:36 Dr. Eva Müller: Eva - I'll be taking point on the solutions architecture and security requirements.

00:00:45 Alex Chen: Great. Quick agenda, we'll do intros, overview of Redwood product offering (hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, private/VPC and on-prem), then dig into what QuantumCore is looking for, their constraints, and then propose a pilot flow. Is that okay?
00:00:58 Marco Ruiz: Perfect.

00:01:07 Priya Patel: I'll try to keep the product bits succinct. So Redwood is a developer-first inference platform — hosted API for quick time to value, dedicated for reserved throughput, and private VPC deployments for regulated customers. We optimize for latency, unit-cost, and reliability. We also have tooling for observability and model rollouts.
00:01:29 Lina Zhao: When you say private/VPC, is that fully customer-managed network or do you maintain any control plane?
00:01:37 Priya Patel: Good question — for our Private offering we typically do a customer-managed network with a lightweight control plane that can be hosted in the customer's VPC or on-prem. You can choose whether to give us access for ops. For enterprise customers we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs.
00:01:55 Dr. Eva Müller: Are you SOC 2 / ISO certs? We're strict about compliance for certain telco and finance customers.
00:02:01 Alex Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II; we're working through ISO processes as well. We'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 report under NDA.
00:02:09 Marco Ruiz: Good. On our side, QuantumCore runs GPU clusters (A100/H100 equivalents, custom interconnect). We're looking at how we can partner—both channel (we want to offer Redwood as preferred inference runtime to our customers) and also tighter technical integrations so Redwood can certify on our hardware.
00:02:30 Priya Patel: That sounds aligned. A couple of quick qualification questions — what are your customers' typical latency expectations and throughput? Are they more batch/async embedding workloads or low-latency chat?
00:02:42 Lina Zhao: Mostly low-latency chat and some high-throughput embedding pipelines for search. Some customers will need sub-100ms token latency for short responses, which is challenging on bigger models.
00:02:55 Priya Patel: Understood. For sub-100ms token latency we often recommend model+kernel tuning and possibly dedicated capacity with NVLink for throughput; caching/prefix caching also helps for repeated prompt prefixes.
00:03:12 Dr. Eva Müller: On the network side, we will need to vet how tokens and request logs are stored. We require KMS + customer-managed keys and at-rest encryption. Also SSO/SAML and RBAC for operational access.
00:03:26 Alex Chen: Yep, we support customer KMS integrations, SAML SSO, and RBAC. We also have configurable data retention policies and can do private inference with no logs retained centrally if needed. We'll send the security checklist.
00:03:41 Marco Ruiz: Great. Curious about pricing tiers and revenue share models for channel partners?
00:03:46 Alex Chen: There are a few ways — for Dedicated/Private we do committed capacity contracts; for hosted API it's usage-based. For channel partners we have referral fees and co-sell arrangements — I can share the partner program doc.
00:03:58 Lina Zhao: From the integration perspective, do you have an SDK or is it just REST?
00:04:03 Priya Patel: REST + SDKs, and we support streaming and function/tool-calling primitives. For partner infra certification, we usually do a short benchmark kit to validate throughput and latency on target hardware.
00:04:17 Dr. Eva Müller: How invasive is the benchmark? Does it require us to provision dedicated nodes or can it run on existing multi-tenant pools?
00:04:25 Priya Patel: We can do both. For preliminary results we can run against a staging multi-tenant pool. For final certification we prefer dedicated capacity so we can control variables like kernel selection and quantization.
00:04:38 Marco Ruiz: Ok. Another item — some of our customers are regulated and need data residency in EU. Do you have region controls for hosting?
00:04:47 Alex Chen: We do. Redwood supports region pinning and can deploy private control planes in customer regions. We also support on-prem installs for air-gapped environments.
00:04:58 Lina Zhao: Excellent. On the technical side, what telemetry do you need from our side for benchmarks? GPU telemetry, interconnect metrics, network latency?
00:05:07 Priya Patel: At minimum GPU utilization, memory usage, PCIe/NVLink metrics, kernel durations, and end-to-end request latency and token latency. If you can provide an infra diagram showing tenancy and network hops that helps a lot.
00:05:23 Dr. Eva Müller: We'll compile that. Also, license and export controls — some of our nodes are in APAC, some in EU; we need clarity on any model licensing restrictions.
00:05:34 Alex Chen: We'll surface model licensing constraints — especially for certain foundation models — and map compatible model variants during the pilot. We'll also propose fallback model variants in case of capacity constraints.
00:05:47 Marco Ruiz: What's the typical pilot timeline you recommend?
00:05:50 Priya Patel: We usually do a 6-8 week pilot: week 0 onboarding and infra exchange, weeks 1-2 baseline benchmarks on your infra, weeks 3-4 tuning (batching/quantization/kernel), and weeks 5-6 final validation and go/no-go. But can compress to 4 weeks if both teams are aligned.
00:06:06 Lina Zhao: Can Redwood run a small POC where we test embedding workloads and a chat flow? We'd like to see token latency distribution.
00:06:13 Priya Patel: Absolutely. We'll need sample prompts, dataset sizes, and expected QPS. We'll prepare a benchmark checklist.
00:06:20 Dr. Eva Müller: On security, we'll want to run a threat model review during the pilot — basic checklist up front and deeper review if pilot goes well.
00:06:28 Alex Chen: Sounds good. We'll share our security checklist and SOC2 under NDA.
00:06:33 Marco Ruiz: From GTM, we'd want co-branded collateral and a joint case study after a successful pilot. Also interested in joint sales plays for HPC and enterprise ML teams.
00:06:44 Alex Chen: We can support that — Redwood marketing and partner ops will coordinate.
00:06:50 Priya Patel: Quick note on technical fallbacks — for customers needing low latency but low cost we sometimes route requests to smaller quantized model variants and use KV cache to reduce token costs. That's something we can demo during the deep-dive.
00:07:04 Lina Zhao: Nice. Any immediate red flags on your side about our infra?
00:07:08 Priya Patel: Not yet — based on the high level description your hardware looks compatible. We'll need the infra diagram and we'll triage any network/NAT/firewall needs.
00:07:18 Alex Chen: Ok, next steps recap: I'll send the partner one-pager and program details; Priya will send benchmark checklist and propose times for a 60-90 minute deep-dive; QuantumCore will share infra diagram, tenancy/security requirements, and introduce legal POC for NDA.
00:07:33 Marco Ruiz: Yep, we'll get those items together.
00:07:36 Dr. Eva Müller: Expect the diagram and initial security notes by next week.
00:07:41 Alex Chen: Great. Any other questions?
00:07:44 Lina Zhao: Not from me.
00:07:46 Marco Ruiz: All good.
00:07:48 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite for the deep-dive.
00:07:54 (crosstalk and small goodbyes)
